questions.scenario: Your teacher assigns a massive group project. What is your natural instinct?

options.text: Breaking down the topic and creating the slides so the information is perfectly clear.
Making sure everyone in the group has a task they actually enjoy doing.
Helping the one group member who is struggling to understand their part.
Taking charge of the overarching theme and directing how the final presentation will look.

questions.scenario: A new student joins your class mid-semester and looks totally lost. What do you do?

options.text: Share my well-organized notes and highlight exactly what they need to study.
Introduce them to different friend groups so they feel included immediately.
Have a quiet, one-on-one chat during lunch to make sure they aren't overwhelmed.
Talk to the principal about setting up an official 'buddy system' for all future new students.

questions.scenario: You are trying to teach your friends a complex new board game. How do you approach it?

options.text: I read the rulebook and create a simplified, step-by-step cheat sheet for everyone.
I focus on hyping everyone up and keeping the energy fun, even if we make mistakes.
I watch to see if anyone is getting frustrated and gently guide them through their turn.
I end up tweaking the rules to make the game faster, better, and more exciting.

questions.scenario: If you had to run a popular Instagram or YouTube channel, what would the content be?

options.text: Highly aesthetic, easy-to-understand carousels explaining complex science or history.
Vlogs about community events, interviews, and bringing diverse people together.
A safe-space channel discussing mental health, sharing advice, and reading subscriber DMs.
A campaign channel focused on rallying thousands of people to fix a major global issue.

questions.scenario: A close friend calls you crying after a huge argument with their parents. What is your response?

options.text: I research and send them articles or books on how to navigate family conflict.
I organize a group hangout with our friend circle to distract them and cheer them up.
I listen patiently for hours without interrupting or judging, letting them vent.
I help them map out a strategic plan to confront their parents and fix the root problem.

questions.scenario: Your school's 'Debate Club' is dying because nobody wants to join. How do you save it?

options.text: Rewrite the training materials so debating seems less intimidating and more fun.
Throw a big pizza party event to attract a massive crowd and recruit new members.
Talk to ex-members individually to understand why they felt insecure or left the club.
Completely rebrand it into a 'Future Leaders Society' and launch it with a grand vision.

questions.scenario: What bothers you the most in your daily life?

options.text: Badly explained instructions, messy notes, or disorganized information.
Seeing someone sitting completely alone and being excluded by a group.
People being incredibly harsh, judgmental, or lacking basic empathy.
People complaining about the system without actually stepping up to fix it.

questions.scenario: You have to spend a Saturday volunteering. Which task do you choose?

options.text: Designing the worksheets and activities for a children's weekend class.
Going door-to-door in a neighborhood to spread awareness about a health drive.
Sitting with the elderly at a care home and listening to their personal stories.
Organizing the entire volunteer schedule, managing the budget, and leading the team.

questions.scenario: If you could have one superpower, what would it be?

options.text: The ability to instantly transfer complex knowledge into anyone's brain.
The ability to instantly speak any language and connect with any culture.
The ability to absorb and instantly heal someone's emotional pain.
The ability to mobilize and inspire millions of people with a single speech.

questions.scenario: You are watching a documentary. What is it most likely about?

options.text: How the human brain learns, memory hacks, or educational psychology.
A grassroots social movement that united a fractured community.
An intimate psychological portrait of teenagers overcoming severe trauma.
An inspiring biography of a visionary leader who built a global charity from scratch.

Curriculum_Designer.title: Curriculum Designer / EdTech Creator
Curriculum_Designer.primary_match_text: You are a master of structure and clarity. You love organizing information, breaking down complex ideas, and making learning accessible for everyone.
Curriculum_Designer.day_in_the_life: Designing interactive lessons for apps, writing textbooks, and creating educational modules that make difficult subjects fun and easy to understand.
Curriculum_Designer.alternative_match_text: Because you have a knack for explaining things perfectly, working in instructional design or educational technology is a strong alternative for you.
Curriculum_Designer.roadmap: Take Humanities or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Education (B.Ed), Psychology, or Instructional Design, and build skills in EdTech software.

Community_Outreach_Manager.title: Community Outreach Coordinator
Community_Outreach_Manager.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate social connector. You thrive on bringing people together, fostering inclusion, and rallying groups behind a shared, positive cause.
Community_Outreach_Manager.day_in_the_life: Organizing awareness camps in rural areas, coordinating massive volunteer networks, and bridging the gap between marginalized communities and educational resources.
Community_Outreach_Manager.alternative_match_text: Since you love organizing people and events for a greater good, managing community relations for large non-profits is a perfect backup plan.
Community_Outreach_Manager.roadmap: Take Humanities in 11th/12th. Pursue a Bachelor of Social Work (BSW), Sociology, or Mass Communication degree.

Youth_Counselor.title: Youth Counselor / Special Educator
Youth_Counselor.primary_match_text: You are deeply empathetic and emotionally intelligent. You naturally pick up on people's feelings and excel at providing a safe, non-judgmental space for others.
Youth_Counselor.day_in_the_life: Conducting 1-on-1 sessions with students, helping them overcome learning barriers, navigating mental health challenges, and advocating for their personal well-being.
Youth_Counselor.alternative_match_text: If you prefer deep, one-on-one connections over large crowds, a career in clinical psychology or special education will fulfill your need to help others directly.
Youth_Counselor.roadmap: Take Humanities with Psychology in 11th/12th. Pursue a BA in Psychology followed by an MA in Counseling or Clinical Psychology.

Education_NGO_Founder.title: Education NGO Founder / Program Director
Education_NGO_Founder.primary_match_text: You are a visionary leader who wants to change the system. You are ambitious, strategic, and not afraid to take charge to solve massive social problems.
Education_NGO_Founder.day_in_the_life: Pitching to global donors, scaling literacy programs across hundreds of schools, hiring passionate teams, and driving the strategic vision of an organization.
Education_NGO_Founder.alternative_match_text: With your leadership skills and drive for impact, running large-scale humanitarian programs or starting a social enterprise is an excellent path.
Education_NGO_Founder.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Social Entrepreneurship, Public Policy, or Business Administration, and start volunteering in leadership roles early.
